record_body:
Account summary (Acme AI)
- Building agentic workflows for customer support + internal knowledge search; cost sensitivity is high because they run long-context summarization + multi-turn chat.
- Primary ask: cost/token reduction without breaking output quality, plus *tight control plane knobs* (route-level enable/disable; no tenant-wide defaults for v1).
- Very interested in Quantization Profile Library as an opt-in beta. They repeatedly said: "we need to be able to turn it off fast per route" and "we need to prove no quality regression on our own prompts." 

Current evaluation posture
- Considering Redwood Hosted API for initial ramp; likely moving key traffic to Dedicated in Q2 for predictable throughput + isolation.
- Wants to start with 1–2 routes only (high-volume summarization route and embeddings/doc-search route later).

Requirements / constraints (from calls + notes)
- Workloads:
  - Chat + summarization (streaming responses required)
  - Some doc-search reranking (future; not in current POC scope)
- Performance targets (soft targets; they’ll validate during canary):
  - p95 end-to-end latency: do not regress > ~5–10% on the summarization route
  - Throughput: cares more about stable tail latency than max tokens/sec
- Cost goals:
  - Target 20–35% cost/token improvement on the top route to justify switching from current provider.
- Controls:
  - Route-level quantization profile selection (explicit profile ref, not silent auto-updates)
  - Region control (nice-to-have): enable first in one region, expand after pass
  - Deterministic selection + clear fallback behavior (baseline precision if incompatible)
- Security/compliance:
  - Audit logging for config changes (must capture actor + before/after)
  - KMS-backed key management for any dedicated/VPC path
  - Retention controls (requests/logs) for regulated customers they serve

Key notes (CRM-style)
- 2025-02-06 technical deep dive (Fireflies link)
  - Asked about “compatibility guardrails”: GPU SKU differences, max context limits, and what happens if profile is incompatible.
  - Concerned about cache interactions: "If kv cache changes, do we get weird latency tails?"
  - Action item: Redwood to confirm metrics emitted include quant_profile_id + applied/fallback.
- 2025-02-19 async follow-ups
  - Asked whether profiles are part of Optimize packaging or included as platform feature. (We told them beta is allowlisted; pricing TBD for GA.)
- 2025-03-05 beta check-in (Fireflies link)
  - Early results: meaningful cost reduction on one test route; saw slight output differences on a small prompt slice.
  - They want an A/B eval playbook they can run with their own prompts + Redwood’s guardrails thresholds.
  - Emphasized rollback: "We can’t have a bad profile version roll through and surprise us." Wants explicit version pinning.

Activity timeline (recent)
- 2025-01-22 — Company created in CRM after inbound interest in cost optimization + dedicated capacity.
- 2025-02-06 — Quantization profile library technical deep dive (SE + Applied ML joined). Fireflies logged.
- 2025-02-11 — Sent beta overview + high-level schema notes; Acme agreed to be design partner if route-level controls + kill-switch exist.
- 2025-02-21 — Internal leadership alignment on risk review / kill-switch approach (see Gmail thread).
- 2025-03-01 — Docs review thread started (Acme requested customer-facing “how to evaluate + rollback” section).
- 2025-03-05 — Beta rollout check-in; planning 1% canary on a single route.
- 2025-03-12 — Updated evaluation plan: proceed with canary pending compatibility matrix + audit log visibility in Console.

Open questions / next steps
- Confirm dedicated GPU SKU for their Q2 sizing + which quant profiles are supported on that SKU.
- Set up 1% canary with explicit rollback criteria (fallback_rate, quality regressions, p95 latency deltas).
- Provide a short compatibility matrix + recommended profile pinning guidance.

Risks
- If quality regressions show up in Acme’s domain prompts, they will stop the beta unless rollback is trivial and audit trails are complete.
- They are wary of any “recommended/latest alias” that can change behavior without an explicit config update.
